plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit whenever you win. Shading the bid down only reduces the chance of winning profitable auctions without lowering the price paid. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid here, unlike first-price auctions. Thus, I will bid my true value of $34 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids, and you pay only the second-highest bid, never overpaying. Shading down doesn't help since payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (unless you're bidding to influence winning probability). With value $45, I'll bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit without risk of overpaying.
